messages.content: i opened my book at the library and found that a page was gone. can you help me tell the teacher?
you could say: a page is gone from my book. i found the problem when i opened it at the library. could i use another book to read that part?
i do not know whether the page was already gone when i took the book.
then do not say when it was lost. your message says when you found the problem, which you do know.
should i say that someone took it?
no. a page being gone does not tell you who took it or how it was lost. you can explain what you saw without adding a reason.
make the message shorter and keep the request for another book.
a page is gone from my book. could i use another book to read that part?
what if the teacher asks which page?
show the pages before and after the part that is gone. if you can see a page number, give that number. you do not need to make one up.
tell me a story in which a child helps her father by reading rather than building.

a father builds a small shelf for books. his daughter wants to help, but she does not know how to build it. she finds the plan on the table and reads each line to him. when a line is not clear, they stop and look at the picture together. she reads slowly, and he listens. at the end, he puts the first book on the shelf. she says that she did not build anything. he says that her reading helped him do the work.
why did they stop at the hard line?
they wanted to understand the plan before doing more work. going slowly at that point helped them keep their work in the right order.
did she learn to build the shelf by herself?
the story does not say that. she helped by reading the plan and looking at the picture with her father.
write what she might say about her part in the work.
i read the plan to my father. when we did not understand a line, we looked at the picture together. i helped with the reading.
there are two cups on the desk. neither cup is mine. does that mean they are yours?
no. knowing that neither cup is yours does not tell us who has them. another person could have them.
use words from my sentence to explain neither.
neither cup is mine says that this cup is not mine and the other cup is not mine.
what if one cup is mine and one is hers?
then neither cup is mine would be wrong. you could say: one cup is mine, and the other is hers.
i am writing a story. make a short conversation about finding the right cup.
is this cup yours? no, mine is the blue cup near the book. then is the white cup hers? i do not know. we should ask her before taking it.
can the people know the color without knowing who has the cup?
yes. they can see that a cup is white without knowing whose cup it is.
explain the difference between the shop opens at nine and the worker opens the shop at nine.
the first sentence says what happens to the shop at nine. the other sentence also says who does it. the worker is the person opening the shop.
write a short story with both ideas, but do not say the same thing again and again.
the worker cleans the floor before nine. she looks at the door and puts her book under the desk. at nine, she opens the shop. a person waiting outside comes in and asks for a card.
what work did she do before opening?
she cleaned the floor, checked the door, and put her book under the desk.
was the person already inside while she cleaned?
no. the story says that the person was waiting outside and came in after she opened the shop.
change the story so the shop is still closed at nine.
the worker cleans the floor before nine. at nine, she finds that she cannot open the door. the shop is still closed, and a person waits outside.
my sister plays music while i study. i want quiet, but i do not want to say she is doing something wrong.
you can ask for what you need: could we have a quiet hour? i am studying, and it is hard for me to read with music playing.
she studies with music herself. does that make my request wrong?
no. people can need different things when they study. she may enjoy music while reading, and you may need quiet. you can explain your need without saying that everyone must study your way.
what could we do if she wants music and i need quiet at the same time?
you could study in different rooms if there is space. you could also choose a quiet hour together, then have music later. ask which choice works for both of you.
write a reply if she says she can stop until lunch.
thank you. a quiet morning will help me finish this part. we can talk again after lunch.
we have six vegetables for two meals. i keep four for dinner and two for lunch. how many are left for another meal?
there are no vegetables left for another meal if all six are being kept for those two meals. four for dinner and two for lunch use the whole group of six.
but there are still six on the table.
yes. they are still on the table because you have not used them yet. keeping food for a meal changes your plan for it, even while the food is in the same place.
so no vegetables left does not always mean no vegetables here?
right. here you can say: there are six vegetables here, but all six are for lunch and dinner. there are no vegetables free for another meal.
write a question that would make that difference clear.
how many vegetables are here, and how many can we use for another meal?
answer that question with my plan.
there are six vegetables here. four are for dinner and two are for lunch, so there are no vegetables free for another meal.
write a story about a grandmother who changes what she thinks about a day after looking at a picture.

a grandmother holds an old picture while her son sits next to her. she says that they went to the park on a cold morning. he looks at the picture and sees a meal on the table. he asks whether they went in the evening. she looks again and can remember dinner before their walk. she says that she had the wrong part of the day in mind. they keep looking at the picture and talk about the people who were there.
does seeing a meal alone tell them that it was evening?
no. people have meals in the morning too. her memory of dinner before the walk gives them another reason to think it was evening.
make the son ask without telling her that she must be wrong.
could it have been evening? i remember that we had dinner before we went for a walk.
why is that a useful question?
it gives her another detail to think about. it also leaves room for them to look at the picture and remember together.
when i say my uncle fixes the clock, am i saying that he changes time?
no. you are saying that he works on the clock so that it works again. a clock helps people tell the time. fixing a broken clock does not change time itself.
write a small story where this difference is important.

a child sees her uncle fixing a clock. she asks if lunch will come later because the clock has stopped. he says that lunch is still at the same time. the clock has stopped working, but the rest of the day is going on. they look at another clock to see how long they have before lunch.
what if there is no other clock in the house?
they could ask someone for the time or look at a phone if one is there. the story would need to say which choice they use.
change the last sentence so they ask a neighbor.
they ask a neighbor for the time so they know how long they have before lunch.
use although in a sentence about waiting for a friend.
although she is ready to leave, she waits for her friend.
is she ready or not?
she is ready. although gives that fact along with another fact: she waits. being ready does not mean she leaves at once.
make it a short conversation between the two friends.
are you ready to go? yes, but i can wait while you finish your page. thank you. i only need a minute. that is fine. i will read the note by the door while i wait.
does the friend ask her to leave without him?
no. he thanks her and says that he needs a minute. the conversation does not have a request for her to go alone.
write a sentence with however about the same idea.
she is ready to leave. however, she waits while her friend finishes his page.
which sentence says why she waits?
the sentence with however says that she waits while her friend finishes his page. that gives more detail than the first sentence.
help me write about a garment i found. it is green and was under a chair. i do not know whose it is.
you could say: i found a green garment under a chair. is anyone looking for it?
should i say it was lost?
you can say where you found it without saying why it was there. someone may have put it there and still know where it is.
what if a person says they are looking for a blue garment?
that does not sound like the green garment you found. you can say: this one is green. could yours be in another place?
i want to ask the group without giving every detail at once.
you could ask: is anyone looking for a garment? if someone says yes, ask them about its color and where they last had it.
why ask them about its color?
their answer can help you check whether you are talking about the same garment. a general yes gives less information.
write a short story where a husband and wife make dinner together and each person has different work.

the husband cooks rice while his wife washes vegetables. she puts the clean vegetables on a plate and brings it to the table. he looks at the rice and asks her to get two cups. she gets the cups, and he brings water. when dinner is ready, they sit together. each person has done part of the work.
who washes the vegetables?
the wife washes the vegetables.
who brings water?
the husband brings water.
change the story so she cooks rice and he washes vegetables. keep the other work the same.

the wife cooks rice while her husband washes vegetables. she puts the clean vegetables on a plate and brings it to the table. he looks at the rice and asks her to get two cups. she gets the cups, and he brings water. when dinner is ready, they sit together. each person has done part of the work.
can he check the rice even though she cooks it?
yes. they can help with different parts of dinner. looking at the rice does not mean he did all the cooking.
what does shall we read together mean?
it is a way to ask another person if they want to read with you. you are asking about doing something together.
give me a reply that says yes but asks for a little time.
yes, i would like that. can we start after i finish this page?
and a reply that says no for today but keeps the idea open?
i cannot today, but i would like to read with you another day. could we try tomorrow?
write a conversation where the people choose tomorrow morning.
shall we read together today? i cannot today. could we try tomorrow? yes. would morning work for you? morning would be good. shall we meet at the library? yes, i will bring my book.
what have they chosen, and what do they still not know?
they have chosen tomorrow morning at the library. they have not chosen a specific hour in that conversation.
